issue.name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
issue.issueBackground: XML external entity injection occurs when XML input containing a reference to an external entity is processed by a weakly configured XML parser.
issue.remediationBackground: Configure the XML parser to disable DTDs (external entities) completely according to OWASP XXE Prevention guidance.
issue.issueDetail: The application parsed an XML document containing external entity references and returned root directory contents in the response body.

issue.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
issue.issueBackground: CSRF vulnerabilities arise when applications rely solely on automatically submitted browser credentials (such as cookies) without unpredictable challenge tokens.
issue.remediationBackground: Implement anti-CSRF tokens (Synchronizer Token Pattern or SameSite=Strict cookies) on all state-modifying requests.
issue.issueDetail: No CSRF token was validated when submitting sensitive state change POST requests.

issue.name: Password Field Submitted using HTTP GET
issue.issueBackground: Submitting sensitive credentials via HTTP GET query parameters causes passwords to be recorded in browser history, server access logs, and HTTP Referer headers.
issue.remediationBackground: Ensure credentials are only transmitted inside HTTP POST request bodies with appropriate Content-Type.
issue.issueDetail: Query parameter 'pwd' was observed in GET request URL.
